validityCheck.title: Denormalization truncation to zero allows free yield extraction with low-decimal reward tokens

checks.notes: References USDC (6 decimals) but issue is about protocol arithmetic, not token non-standard behavior
Root cause in StableYieldAccumulator.sol lines 607, 675, 699, 704 -- all in scope

checks.evidence: Root cause is integer division truncation in _denormalizeAmount() at line 704, which is the denormalization step of the normalize-discount-denormalize pipeline. Known issue #2 explicitly covers 'Decimal normalization precision loss (documented design choice)'. The zero-amount edge case is the extreme manifestation of the same truncation, not a distinct vulnerability.
checks.matchedKnownIssue: Decimal normalization precision loss (documented design choice)

validityCheck.notes: The finding acknowledges prior L-01 identified dust-level truncation and argues this is a 'qualitative escalation' because actualPayment becomes exactly zero. However, truncation-to-zero is the extreme case of the documented precision loss design choice. The root cause (integer division in denormalization) is identical. The project documented decimal normalization precision loss as an accepted design choice, which inherently includes the zero boundary.
validityCheck.recommendation: Remove from submission. Root cause overlaps with known issue #2.

validityCheck.title: Raw approve() call in ClaimArbitrage permanently blocks execution for USDT-like reward tokens

checks.notes: Finding is about USDT's non-standard approve behavior. USDT is the explicit C4 exception -- USDT findings are VALID.

This is NOT the approve race condition. The approve race is about front-running between approve and transferFrom. This finding is about USDT's requirement to reset allowance to zero before setting a new non-zero value, causing a permanent revert.
Setting USDT as reward token is a reasonable admin action -- USDT is a major stablecoin and the contract documentation references it in examples.
Root causes in ClaimArbitrage.sol line 184 and StableYieldAccumulator.sol line 482 -- both in scope
Does not match any of the 8 known issues. Known issue #5 (front-running of setRewardToken) is a different attack vector.

validityCheck.notes: No invalid patterns detected. USDT is the explicit C4 exception to the non-standard token rule. The contract imports SafeERC20 but uses raw approve() at the affected lines, which is a genuine code defect. The fix (forceApprove) is straightforward and the impact (permanent bricking) is significant.
